Bursa Malaysia Ends Slightly Higher on Bargain-Hunting

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – Bursa Malaysia staged a slight recovery on Friday, October 2, 2026, as bargain-hunting emerged following a recent sharp sell-off. However, the rebound lacked strong upward momentum as broader Asian markets remained under pressure ahead of crucial United States labour market data releases. At the 5:00 PM close, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose marginally by 0.51 points, or 0.03 per cent, to end at 1,630.87 compared to Thursday’s close of 1,630.36.

Daily Newswatch - 25 Sep 2026

The FBM KLCI ended 0.2% lower to 1,672.3 points on Thursday, as renewed oil-price gains and elevated global bond yields pressured investor sentiment, offsetting intermittent buying interest in selected counters. Telecommunications & Media (-2.0%), Technology (-1.8%) and Consumer Product and Services (-0.4%) led sectoral losses, with Press Metal Aluminium (-1.7%), YTL Power International (-1.9%) and Petronas Gas (-0.6%) among the key laggards. Market breadth, however, was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 677 to 436, and 542 counters unchanged.

RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4pct

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, according to RHB Group. In RHB's Global Economics Outlook for Q4 2026, group chief economist and head of market research, Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures.

text:
Public Bank, Maybank and CIMB Among Eight Malaysian Banks on Forbes’ Global List

Eight Malaysian banks made Forbes’ inaugural ranking of the world’s top-performing banks in 2026. Public Bank ranked fifth in Tier 2, the highest position among Malaysia’s three entries in the category. Maybank placed 14th while CIMB Group Holdings ranked 35th. Tier 2 covers banks with assets from US$100 billion to US$500 billion. Hong Leong Financial Group ranked ninth in Tier 3 while RHB Bank placed 37th. The category covers banks with assets from US$50 billion to US$100 billion. Bank Rakyat placed 32nd in Tier 4 while AmBank Group ranked 68th.
notes: 'Tier 2/3/4' dropped (categories, not dates - model had tagged as DATE). Money range split into separate amounts: 'US$100 billion', 'US$500 billion', 'US$50 billion' (model had one span 'US$100 billion to US$500 billion'). text:
How should FIs build and sustain digital trust when AI is transforming the threat landscape?

Artificial intelligence (AI) has become one of the defining technologies shaping the future of financial services. Banks are embedding AI into customer service, credit assessment, payments, fraud detection, wealth management, software development and internal operations at an unprecedented pace. The rapid emergence of generative AI (Gen AI) and increasingly autonomous AI agents has further accelerated adoption, bringing forward productivity gains that many institutions had previously expected only later in the decade.

text:
Bursa Malaysia Stays Lower at Mid-Morning Trailed by Heavyweight Selling

Bursa Malaysia remained firmly in negative territory at mid-morning on Thursday, October 1, 2026, dragged down by selling pressure across key blue-chip counters, primarily in healthcare, industrial products, and utilities sectors. At 11:00 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 11.73 points to 1,639.44 compared to Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The index had opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth was negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 484 to 273, while 460 counters traded unchanged, 1,556 untraded, and 12 suspended.

text:
Maybank 2Q FY26 Net Profit Rises 2.4% to RM2.69 Billion

Maybank reported a 2.4% year-on-year increase in net profit to RM2.69 billion for the second quarter of FY2026, supported by stronger core fee income, tighter cost control and lower impairment provisions. The banking group also recorded profit before tax of RM3.64 billion, representing a 3.7% increase from the corresponding quarter last year. Return on equity improved to 12.0%, compared with 11.6% a year earlier, while net operating income reached RM7.51 billion. For the first six months of FY2026, Maybank generated RM5.17 billion in net profit.

text:
Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says - Newswav

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).

Daily Newswatch - 1 Oct 2026

The FBM KLCI rebounded 0.4% to 1,651 points on Wednesday after the previous day’s sharp selloff as caution appeared to persist on equities amid a mixed backdrop on the broader Asian markets with rising international bond yields, particularly US 10-year Treasury yields. Construction (+2.07%), Utilities (+0.6%) and Property (+0.4%) led sectoral gains, led by Nestle Malaysia (+1.1%), Tenaga Nasional (+1.9%) and Petronas Gas (+1.3%). Market breadth remained weak, with 695 losers against 410 gainers, while 583 counters were unchanged.

Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah to hold wedding receptions in Muar & Kota Kinabalu, public invited to 'Kenduri Rakyat'

Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and Malaysian singer-actress Bella Astillah, who are set to marry on Oct 10, will celebrate their special occasion with the public through two receptions themed “Kenduri Rakyat”.  The couple, who got engaged on March 28, will first exchange vows at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur.  The celebrations will then continue in Muar, Johor, on Oct 25, before the couple heads to Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on Oct 31.

text:
Maybank Falls Below RM10 for First Time in Nine Months as Rising Bond Yields Hurt Banking Stocks

KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Investors may also demand higher returns on corporate bonds, affecting appetite for new issuances.

text:
Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google

SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Gold Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses.  In her brief judgment on Wednesday, Justice Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business.  The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors.
